open_points.subject: store.open_store SQLite database opening
open_points.text: “the start's walk finds no link before the database is opened”
open_points.question: What must happen if the database path or an SQLite auxiliary path is replaced with a symbolic link between the start-time walk and SQLite opening it?
options: Trust that no process using the kernel's user changes the directory
After SQLite opens the file, verify that it is the same non-link object observed by the walk
Use a SQLite opening mechanism that binds the checked object to the open
open_points.default_guess: Verify the opened database and auxiliary files against the start-time observations and stop startup on any mismatch.

open_points.subject: later SQLite store calls
open_points.text: “The database file and its journal are opened by SQLite, which Python cannot ask to refuse a link” versus “A link found later makes that store call fail with nothing written” and “symlink_inside(data_directory) -> refused”
open_points.question: If the database or journal path becomes a symbolic link after startup, is the next SQLite store call required to detect it and fail without writing, or are SQLite-managed paths exempt from the later-link rule?
options: The later-link rule includes SQLite-managed paths
SQLite-managed paths are exempt and may be followed
SQLite-managed paths are exempt only under an explicit trusted-host assumption
open_points.default_guess: Treat SQLite-managed paths as included and perform a pre-call identity/link check, although the text does not specify an atomic way to preserve the nothing-written guarantee.

open_points.subject: SQLite-managed files
open_points.text: “The database file and its journal are opened by SQLite”
open_points.question: Which SQLite-created files are covered by “its journal,” and which are exempt from the store's O_NOFOLLOW rule: rollback journal, WAL, shared-memory file, temporary database files, or another fixed set under a fixed journal mode?
options: Fix rollback-journal mode and exempt only the database and `-journal` files
Fix WAL mode and exempt the database, `-wal`, and `-shm` files
Exempt every path SQLite may create or open
open_points.default_guess: Use SQLite's default rollback-journal mode and treat only the database and rollback-journal paths as SQLite-managed.

open_points.subject: sandbox.probe_sandbox host qualification
open_points.text: “on any other the sandbox probe of the start sequence (A03) fails and the start stops, and any Linux on which that probe passes is a host” while A03 specifies only that “one probe execution succeeds”
open_points.question: What exact facilities must the probe exercise before a Linux system qualifies as a supported host, and what guarantees that the probe fails on every non-Linux host without an explicit host test?
options: A minimal function execution is sufficient and packaging prevents non-Linux execution
The probe must exercise every required Linux mechanism, including namespaces, mounts, limits, pidfd handling, cleanup and descriptor passing
The probe must additionally perform an explicit operating-system check
open_points.default_guess: Make the probe exercise every required sandbox mechanism and rely on those Linux-specific operations, rather than an explicit platform-name test, to reject unsupported hosts.
